item.title: Training Framework
item.description:
MARLHF and MADPO share one training framework. Actors generate joint responses, the task reward ranks them into preference pairs, and the iterative trainers repeat this against a comparator, with a replay buffer selecting the pairs for each update. This page covers the actor layouts, the iterative loop, the comparator, and replay; MARLHF and MADPO describe the two learning objectives.

Collaboration Modes#

collaboration_mode sets the trainable actor layout, and comparator_generation_mode sets the comparator layout in iterative training.

item.title: Multi-Agent RLHF
item.description:
Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (MARLHF) fits a joint reward model to preference pairs, then trains the policies with RL on the learned reward. CoMLRL generates the preference labels with the task reward_func.

The training flow is: task items → preference pairs → Stage 1: joint reward learning → Stage 2: policy reinforcement learning. Because the reward model scores the team’s complete response, separate actors learn from one shared reward. MADPO instead optimizes the policies directly on the pairs, without a reward model.

item.title: Multi-Agent DPO
item.description:
Multi-Agent Direct Preference Optimization (MADPO) trains the agents directly on preferred and rejected joint responses, without a reward model or a separate RL stage. Its loss combines all agents’ preference margins, so each policy learns from the team’s outcome.

The training flow is: task items → preference pairs → joint preference loss → policy updates. MARLHF uses the same pairs to fit a joint reward model first and then trains the policies with RL.
